scope: Native TES III Morrowind extension: observed worldlife chronicle with direct NPC conversation, owned actor wandering, live outdoor atmosphere, single-file Windows setup candidate, and earlier dialogue, knowledge and exploration paths
excluded: New World and NWDB code, data and assets
live bridge inbox contents and companion-status state

publicPackageTests.scope: Temporary source/package/launcher fixtures and local HTTP handler tests; no game launch or model download. Native checks are separately scoped in the native verification summary.

limitations: The public source archive contains installer source and own art, but no Bethesda game assets or engine binaries
Public setup candidate needs an existing configured OpenMW installation; private full-engine setup is local-only pending binary dependency and corresponding-source review
One setup EXE and one visible game entry do not make Morrowind's runtime, resources, model weights, or licensed game assets a single file
The public setup needs a previously configured OpenMW profile; the private local full-engine setup can instead bind the user's licensed Data Files directly
Building the setup from source requires .NET 10, Python, Pillow and the verified Python embeddable ZIP; running its self-contained EXE does not require a local compiler
Native gameplay on Linux not tested
Sustained frame rate and every 0.8 mouse/button path remain unverified in the personal game session
No complete quest rewrite, global texture replacement, new landmass or multiplayer service
No separate Unreal game, online server, crypto transaction or Steam submission
No universal compatibility or frame-rate promise
